name: Save the Sun
what_it_is: A deduction game where you out-question an Oracle and race a Gemini-played wolf to name the hidden rune first.
why_it_exists: Proves an AI can be a live, fallible opponent without ever being trusted with the truth.
long_description: A SvelteKit app on Cloud Run where a deterministic engine owns every fact while Gemini interprets Asks, plays the wolf, transcribes speech, and voices both characters — never seeing the secret. Provably winnable every round, keyboard- and screen-reader-complete.
outcome: A spoken Oracle and wolf, and a debug stream that shows the engine, not Gemini, holding the secret. Took Best Google AI Usage at the June Solstice Game Jam 2026.

name: Unearthed
what_it_is: Enter an address, get the coal mine feeding that grid — operator, county, accident record, tons pulled out — then ask about the contract in plain language.
why_it_exists: Power Profiler and iLoveMountains publish aggregates. Neither names the mine behind a given house, or the safety record of the people working it.
long_description: Three tiers: SvelteKit in the browser, FastAPI on Cloud Run, Snowflake as the data and AI spine. MSHA, EIA and EPA records stay in Snowflake — H3 hexbin geospatial and the EPA Clean Air Markets Marketplace feed run natively, with no ETL out. Cortex Analyst turns a typed question into SQL against a semantic model; Cortex Complete on llama3.3-70b writes the memorial prose from the mine's own safety record. With Snowflake down it falls back to nineteen cached subregions and flags the prose as degraded rather than passing a template off as generated.
outcome: Built for the Earth Day 2026 Weekend Challenge, entered under Best Use of Snowflake, named an Overall Winner. Taken down after the challenge rather than kept paying to run it.
image_alt: Unearthed application interface tracing electricity from a user's address to the coal mine feeding their grid

blog_posts.title: Unearthed—The Coal Mine Behind Every Light Switch

name: Happen to Have?
what_it_is: A voice advice exchange where you answer a stranger's question out loud before you're allowed to ask one of your own.
why_it_exists: Makes giving the admission rule instead of an optional extra, and keeps every piece of advice human-authored.
long_description: Next.js 16 on Cloud Run with Neon Postgres, where Gemini transcribes, translates, redacts and judges each recording across four parallel calls that must agree unanimously. The original audio lives only for the length of the request and never reaches storage; publication and the earned ask commit in one SQL statement.
outcome: Shipped live with anonymous sessions, no accounts and no feed. A withheld result explains itself in human-written copy, crisis routes to real support lines, and playback is voiced from processed text so no stranger's real voice is replayed.

name: Carbon Trace

name: Wild Find
what_it_is: An Android scavenger hunt for kids 8 and up, played with a parent: three plants recorded nearby this month, found and photographed, with open-weight models on the phone checking every photo.
why_it_exists: A kid's reason to go outside should not cost a photo or a location. Nothing leaves the phone but the center of a whole-degree square.
long_description: Each hunt asks iNaturalist for plants near the center of a rounded whole-degree area, never the device's coordinates, and picks three targets from different genera, excluding plants flagged toxic. On capture, TinyCLIP checks that the frame is a plant and BioCLIP scores it against the local candidates, both on the phone through ONNX Runtime. The Kotlin rules accept a target's genus only when the scores clear the competing plants and toxic look-alikes. Gemma 4 26B A4B writes hints at build time on a laptop; the app runs no language model. Kid copy never says a plant is safe, and both the pipeline build and the device tests check that.
outcome: v1.0.0 released as a signed APK, built for the DEV Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge: Touch Grass. With the shipped guard, 53 of 99 held-out target photos pass and none of 267 toxic photos passes across the tuning and test sets; the measurements are recorded under docs/results.

name: Soundboard
what_it_is: A release agent for one musician: self-hosted Gemma 4 watches and listens to a finished music video, drafts its YouTube title, description, hashtags and tags, and verifies the upload.
why_it_exists: Nathan writes, records and films his own music; publishing still cost him a marketing department's worth of metadata. Built for him in one weekend, with unreleased audio never leaving our own cloud project.
long_description: A SvelteKit app on Cloud Run drives a page-driven pipeline, one step per request: ffmpeg measures loudness, true peak, clipping and silence, then Gemma 4 12B on llama-server behind a single scale-to-zero Vertex AI L4 endpoint analyzes each 29.5-second audio window plus eight frames from it. The model never gets to invent a number — ffmpeg's measurements are the only ones that reach the draft, and model-emitted numerics are stripped. Hashtags come from a deterministic search of existing videos, the draft is grounded in the genre's most-viewed music videos and Nathan's approved brand guide, and the upload goes up private and is read back from the YouTube API before it is marked verified. One Sentry trace per job, each Gemma call recorded as an AI agent span.
outcome: Live at soundboard.anchildress1.dev, entered in the DEV Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend. One complete draft per video for Nathan to approve, edit or re-run; the model bills about $0.81 an hour while awake and nothing scaled to zero.
image_alt: Soundboard drafting a YouTube title, description and tags from a finished music video

blog_posts.title: 20+ Years of Friendship. One Weekend to Build His Marketing Department.

name: Metal Birds Feed
what_it_is: A private aircraft feed assembled from national civil-aviation registers, normalized to one schema with natural-person street addresses removed.
why_it_exists: I wanted aircraft lookups without a paid aviation API or a separate integration for every country's register.
long_description: FAA is the schema baseline; other registries extend it only when they publish something structurally new, and natural-person street addresses are dropped at the mapping config. Country differences become YAML field mappings instead of one-off parsers. Per-country slices assemble in Cloudflare R2 into one SQLite file baked into a scale-to-zero Cloud Run container for authenticated tail-number and ICAO hex lookups.
outcome: One schema across every source, each recorded under an Open, Private-use, or Restrictive posture in DATA_LICENSES.md — no paid aviation API in the stack.
image_alt: Metal Birds Feed registry unifying aircraft records from global civil aviation authorities into a single normalized schema

name: Vestige
what_it_is: An on-device ADHD brain tracker for Android: 30-second voice entries in, sourced behavioral patterns out. No grading, no gamification.
why_it_exists: On-device ADHD recall, built so nothing — not even your voice — ever leaves the phone.
long_description: Gemma 4 E4B takes native audio (no SpeechRecognizer) and streams transcription plus follow-up, then three background lens passes feed a deterministic Kotlin convergence resolver. EmbeddingGemma drives tone-word drift; a sealed NetworkGate and a verifyNoTelemetry Gradle task make privacy a build-time guarantee, not a promise.
outcome: Gemma 4 Challenge entry. 73% meaningful lens divergence against a 50% bar; 12/12 entries parsed at a 21.2s mean on a Galaxy S24 Ultra.
image_alt: Vestige Android brain tracker surfacing sourced behavioral patterns from on-device Gemma 4 analysis

blog_posts.title: Vestige: A Gemma 4 Brain Tracker That Won't Blow Smoke Up Your Ass

name: RAI Lint
what_it_is: commitlint and gitlint plugins that fail a commit unless it carries an AI attribution footer and a human Signed-off-by line.
why_it_exists: Commits on AI-assisted repos were landing with no record of what the model wrote and what a human reviewed.
long_description: A TypeScript plugin for commitlint and a Python plugin for gitlint check one of five AI-attribution footer levels (Authored-by through Generated-by) and the human Signed-off-by line. A parity test keeps the regexes identical across both languages. The linters check the format; reviewing whether the credit is accurate is still a human job.
outcome: Published to npm and PyPI via OIDC Trusted Publishing and enforced on this repo's own commit hook.
image_alt: RAI Lint banner enforcing explicit AI attribution in git commits and workflows

blog_posts.title: Signing Your Name on AI-Assisted Commits with RAI Footers

name: RAI Commit Badge
what_it_is: A GitHub Action that scores the RAI attribution footers already sitting in your git history and publishes the result as a badge.
why_it_exists: rai-lint makes the footers mandatory. This one reads them back out and puts the number where people can see it.
long_description: Non-merge commits in the adoption window are scored by footer type — Authored-by at 0.00 through Generated-by at 0.90 — and weighted by source churn, while lockfiles and generated output are excluded. The window opens at the earliest RAI footer, and squash-collapsed history is surfaced as degraded granularity in the job summary instead of being passed off as exact.
outcome: Implemented and running against its own repository: the JavaScript action scores repository history, rewrites only the marked README block, reports the score window, commit counts, and squash granularity, and ships as a committed Node 24 bundle. The first release and Marketplace listing are still pending.
image_alt: RAI Commit Badge banner showing an AI attribution score published as a repository badge

name: SupaScribe Notes
what_it_is: A remote MCP server and ChatGPT App on Cloud Run that writes and queries the index cards backing this site's notes.
why_it_exists: Decisions and postmortems died in scratch files unless filing one took a single tool call from whichever editor or chat was already open.
long_description: An Express server exposes seven MCP tools over streaming HTTP. Every write validates against Zod — including the two-level tags hierarchy — before touching Supabase Postgres, records a row in card_revisions on every change, and returns per-card status on batch writes.
outcome: Deployed on Cloud Run and used to file the notes in this portfolio's Algolia index.

name: System Notes
what_it_is: An evidence-first engineering portfolio organized around searchable decisions instead of finished-product theater.
why_it_exists: The useful part of a project is usually the constraint, failure, or choice that produced it. This keeps that reasoning attached to the work.
long_description: A Next.js app with an Algolia-backed decision index and a complete project directory spanning active systems, retired tools, and deliberate dead ends. Every merge clears CI-enforced coverage and Lighthouse budgets before it ships.
outcome: Live at anchildress1.dev as a searchable record of engineering work, deployed on Cloud Run behind unit, browser, accessibility, security, and performance gates.

name: Commit Chronicles
what_it_is: A card generator that reads one public repo's commit history and tells you what you were obsessed with — the 3am streak, the 107-day silence, the return.
why_it_exists: Proves a model can find something true in a commit history without being allowed to invent it.
long_description: Snowflake does all of it. An external access integration pulls the repo from inside the warehouse, fifteen SQL views score six storylines and pick exactly one, and a UDF over AI_COMPLETE narrates that single thread — 20 to 140 commit lines, never the whole history. Thirteen SQL checks run before a card exists, so it fails loudly instead of rendering a lie.
outcome: Live and generating, capped at 140 commit lines per repo. Nothing to say gets a gray card, not a fabrication. Submitted to the DEV Weekend Challenge: Passion Edition.

name: Echo ESLint
what_it_is: A reusable ESLint configuration built for AI-assisted codebases.
why_it_exists: One shared lint boundary that keeps AI agents inside the lines across every repo.
long_description: Echo collapses formatting and linting into a single shared config so the same boundaries apply across projects and agents without restating preferences. Built for AI consumers first, humans second.
outcome: One shared Prettier + ESLint config enforced identically across every repo it's installed in, verified by Node's built-in test runner and SonarCloud.

name: Dev.to Mirror
what_it_is: An automated, AI-optimized mirror of my technical writing.
why_it_exists: Your best writing is invisible to the AI systems that could be citing it. This isn't.
long_description: A Python job on GitHub Actions pulls my DEV posts, renders them through Jinja2 templates optimized for AI parsing, and deploys to Firebase Hosting. Not SEO or analytics — it exists so AI systems can correctly index and cite the work.

name: Multivert
what_it_is: A free, sharable personality quiz that scores you across all five "vert" types — introvert, extrovert, ambivert, omnivert, and otrovert.
why_it_exists: A zero-stakes weekend build to see if I could — the only quiz that includes otrovert.
long_description: A deterministic, fully client-side TypeScript engine scores 35 questions across four axes into five independent fit percentages — the bars don't sum to 100. No backend, no tracking, no persistence. Built with vibes, AI, and a small pile of cited research.
outcome: A deployed, no-stakes quiz on Cloudflare Pages — five independent "vert" scores, cited sources, and zero telemetry.

name: DEV Community Dashboard
what_it_is: A public signal-triage dashboard that routes volunteer attention to the DEV posts the feed would otherwise bury.
why_it_exists: The DEV feed rewards volume. This surfaces the posts a scroll-past would bury instead.
long_description: A Next.js app that pulls the Forem API, then runs each post through a GPT-5 nano-to-mini cascade scoring engagement and conversational signal — not recency — to flag high-need, low-interaction questions before they vanish beneath higher-performing content.
outcome: Ran in production, helping volunteers triage unanswered DEV posts by engagement signal instead of recency. Since retired.

name: Hermes Agent
what_it_is: A personal AI-agent playground exploring memory as a first-class concern.
why_it_exists: A zero-stakes sandbox for getting agent memory wrong on purpose.
long_description: Python and LangChain orchestrate a local agent backed by TimescaleDB + pgvector for memory — Ollama runs locally, OpenAI handles embeddings. Built to watch memory behave, drift, and misbehave, without production pressure shaping the decisions.
outcome: Running locally with a working TimescaleDB/pgvector memory loop. No production numbers — it was never meant to ship, just to watch memory misbehave up close.
